To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the VBNC state induced by abiotic stress in the biocontrol agent Pseudomonas CHA0 does not promote strain persistence in soil.
the viable-but-nonculturale state induced by abiotic stress in the biocontrol agent P. fluorescens CHAO does not promote strain persistence in soil.

VBNC cells of P. fluorescens CHAO-Rif were generated in vitro by exposure to a low redox potential or high salt levels but that they did not display enhanced survival in soil compared with culturable bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of oxygen limitation and low redox potential on the survival of P. fluorescens CHAO-Rif in soil.
the effects of oxygen limitation and high NaCl levels on the VBNC state of the biocontrol inoculant CHA0-RIF.
the fate of the biocontrol agent Pseudomonas sp. strain CHA0-R in the rhizosphere of field-grown wheat and in soil microcosms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in our experimental conditions, the VBNC state induced by oxygen limitation and/or high NaCl levels in vitro did not promote strain persistence in soil.
the VBNC state induced by the abiotic stresses tested here does not promote strain persistence in soil.
, in the case of Pseudomonas, the VBNC state is not a physiological strategy to enhance strain persistence in soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of VBNC cells of P. fluorescens CHAO-Rif in soil was not a consequence of the induction of this physiological state by abiotic stress in vitro, but was due to the presence of culturable cells of CHAORif at the time of soil inoculation.
VBNC cells of P. fluorescens CHAO-Rif are not a survival strategy for the strain in soil.
the VBNC state of P. fluorescens CHAO-Rif does not confer enhanced persistence under the conditions tested.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the VBNC state of CHA0 induced by abiotic stress in vitro did not promote persistence of this strain in soil, which suggests a limited role for the VBNC state in promoting persistence of this biocontrol strain in soil under the conditions tested.
the VBNC state of CHA0 does not promote strain persistence in soil, which may explain why this state has never been observed in the soil environment.

, although the VBNC state can be obtained in the laboratory under abiotic stress conditions that are encountered in the field, this does not necessarily mean that it will confer enhanced survival in soil.
